questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I guess it was rather a mix of the above. Of course, the academic prestige of Cornell made me choose it over other American institutions. Nonetheless, career opportunities and personal/cultural connections to the USA also played a big role.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Academic prestige (It being an Ivy league school)
Proximity to New York City
American culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was nice and easy. We had a briefing and some introductory presentations, which also helped in meeting other international peers.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A comprehensive canvas page, which frankly, included all need to know and nice to know

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We lived in the Beta Theta Pi house (Fraternity). It was technically "on campus" ground, but the lease agreement was not affiliated with Cornell.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen although nobody used it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want to live in a fraternity house, then try reaching out. You will get a lot of no's, but some are very welcoming to boarders.

What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is rather complicated. You do not exactly know what courses you are allowed to apply to. It took a long time to figure out exactly what courses were open to us as KU exchange students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You make a priority list on your own based off courses on student center. Then, at the exact (Not 1 minute after) time when the courses open up for registration, you click. For the more popular courses, it is kind of a lottery whether you get it instantly or get into an endless waitlist.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Canvas, introductory meeting and two people which we could always contact

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I got 3/5 of my priority list. Luckily, a lot of courses were still open.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready by your computer (with good wifi) at the time of registration. Have plan B's. Politely email the professor if student center does not allow you to register for some reason.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can really feel that there is a lot of resources dedicated to each class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I actually both took BA (Undergrad), MA (Graduate) and pHd (Graduate) courses. The difficulties were appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depended on the class. But overall, it was much more interactive. In UCPH, I have experienced plenty of lectures where not a single question was asked during the whole 90 minutes. Even in the larger classes, it was normal for the professors to constantly ask questions for the students. In the smaller classes there could often be spontanous discussions between the professor and the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do game theory with -NAME REDACTED-!!! it is generally a really easy course, but it was really interesting. Most of the classes consists of him just talking with a couple of notes and drawing on the chalkboard. There is barely any mathematics, but he managed to connect the field of game theory to philosophy, litterature and history. questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When it comes to the university there is a good gym, there are like a million clubs (sports, politics, etc), there is a pool, a bowling hall, plenty of food halls, cafes, interesting events and so on. Ithaca (Apart from Cornell) is on the other hand very empty in my opinion.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Rowing club
Go to Argos (bar)
Wine tour (Visit wineyards)
Go see a hockey game
Go see a basketball game
Just walk around, its really a nice campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Of course, NYC. But domestic travel is generally quite affordable in the US, so apart from NYC I would recommend traveling to other big US  cities. Toronto is also quite close.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. As many people say, Americans are quite open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met most people through greek life, which is really prominent. You quickly get to meet a lot of the people from the different fraternities and sororities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think it the small things that just slowly build up. In the beginning I did not really experience any culture shock, but then the small conversational things begin getting more noticable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, the sports culture, the diversity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Lock in during the midterms, they will haunt you afterwards. 

In many courses, a lot of material is available on canvas, so you dont really need books.

In the food halls, you can ask for a green box (or multiple) and fill it food for later. It does not matter what meal plan you have. I found out about this very late.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try as hard as you can to get invited to a wine tour during the beginning of the semester. These are some of the most fun events during the semester.

Get to know some of the guys / girls from greek life. They will help you get into the better events happening on weekends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold, dark and windy winter

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO BIG RED!!!!!!!!

questions.answer: Yes
